properties.description:
When a Decision reaches `accepted` from anything else, or a GOVERNED_BY edge is drawn to an already-accepted Decision, the reply carries a `settled_question_prose` block: each governed node whose prose still asserts the question is open, the phrase that matched, and an excerpt QUOTED AROUND THE MATCH so the reader sees the words that fired rather than the node's opening paragraph.

THE SIBLING OF `cap:a-status-advance-says-whether-its-prose-predates-it`, and built on its reasoning rather than beside it. That one catches a STATUS outrunning its own description inside one node. This one catches PROSE OUTRUNNING A DECISION THAT GOVERNS IT across an edge — the same rot, one relation out.

BOTH TRIGGER MOMENTS ARE COVERED, and that is a design choice with a reason: the decision may be settled first and the edge drawn afterwards, which is the ordering the incident that prompted this actually had available. A hook on the status setter alone would have missed it entirely.

WHY A REPLY AND NOT A DETECTOR, measured before building rather than argued: over reflow2's own design, 43 of 640 nodes governed by an accepted Decision carry one of the nine shipped markers somewhere in their prose, and a good share are legitimate — a node that QUOTES an old question, or discusses a different one in a long statement. As a sweep that is 43 findings of mixed quality, which is the noise that gets switched off in a week. Fired when somebody accepts the decision or draws the edge, it is one node in front of the person who just moved it.

⚠️ HONEST LIMITS, all three real and none hidden.
(1) IT IS LEXICAL. Nine marker phrases, chosen as words any project would write rather than this one's idioms — "that is his call to make" was in the incident and is deliberately NOT a marker, on `rule:reflow2-is-built-for-other-projects-not-for-itself`. It cannot tell an assertion from a quotation of one, and the test file records the moment that limit bit the test's own first draft.
(2) IT NEVER SAYS THE PROSE IS WRONG, per `dec:report-dont-judge` — it names what matched, quotes the text, and asks. A node that quotes an old question is correct and looks identical from the outside; only a person can tell.
(3) IT FIRES WHERE THE DIVERGENCE IS CREATED, NOT WHERE IT IS READ. A session that simply READS a stale node still gets no warning, and the other half of the originating finding — that `search_design` does not surface a governing Decision from a query about the node it governs — is untouched and still true.

📌 THE CALIBRATION FIGURE IS A ONE-OFF, not a standing measurement. It was taken on 2026-09-09 and nothing re-runs it; if the markers start firing on correct nodes as the design grows, the test suite stays green while the instrument becomes noise. An earlier draft of this description quoted 48, measured with a looser marker list than the one that shipped — corrected the same day by re-measuring against the nine actually in the binary. Three of those nine (`to be decided`, `not been decided`, `awaiting a decision`) match nothing in this corpus and are kept as phrases other projects write, not as anything this one has evidence for.
properties.name: A Decision that settles names the prose it governs that still says the question is open
